text:
jessica: quick heads-up — Console folks asked for a per-route header override toggle so product can run header-based experiments without infra changes. can we discuss risks/requirements? :thinking:

raj: short answer: doable but we need guardrails. header overrides are basically an attack surface for routing spoofing. we need server-side validation and telemetry before we expose it in the console.

marta: can you sketch the exact UX they want? is this a one-off checkbox or a rules editor?

jessica: console-team wants a simple toggle + a small rule editor for key/value pairs (e.g., set X-Experiment: betaA). non-dev users should be able to enable an override per-route for up to N minutes.

liam: we already have precedence logic: explicit signed assertion header (x-route-assertion) > x-customer > user-agent heuristics > default. if we let console inject arbitrary headers, it will bypass all heuristics unless we restrict it.

raj: proposal: allow console overrides only for a whitelisted set of headers (X-Experiment, X-Routing-Hint). require the override to be submitted with a signed admin token so it's auditable. server will stamp `x-override-actor` and `x-override-expiry` and reject requests without those when override flag is active.

marta: agree on whitelisting. also need telemetry: show how many requests matched the override, latency delta, and how often it falls back to other variants. product needs that in the rollout panel.

console-team: +1 for telemetry. ask: can we show a one-click revert if routing causes regressions?

raj: yes — implement a circuit-breaker that flips the override off automatically if error-rate or latency crosses threshold. we already have the feature in canary rollouts for model variants; reuse it.

jessica: security question: how do we prevent end-users from spoofing these headers in client requests?

liam: we won't accept raw client-sent override headers. the system will only honor overrides that originate from the console flow and are injected at the edge with an internal signature. any client-supplied same-name header gets dropped unless it carries a valid signature. example rule in edge proxy:

```
# pseudo config
route /api/* {
  match_headers: ["x-customer", "user-agent"]
  override_headers: ["x-experiment", "x-routing-hint"]
  honor_override_if_signed: true
  override_audit_stream: "override-events"
}
```

marta: also add rate limits on how many concurrent override-enabled requests a tenant can have — otherwise product could abuse to get preferential routing. quotas tie into billing too.

raj: agreed. quota check: when override is active, we apply a lightweight quota token with separate accounting so that costs are visible in console. add telemetry tags: override=true, override_actor=<id>, override_tier.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/override-guardrails -> staging at 2024-11-07T14:05Z :rocket:

liam: for rollout UX, show a confidence band in the console (p95 latency, error rate) and allow the user to set thresholds for the circuit-breaker. default thresholds should be conservative.

marta: need one more thing — logging/audit retention. overrides should be kept in audit logs for at least 90 days and surfaced in the per-route change history.

jessica: action items: (1) eng-platform to draft edge validation + config (raj), (2) console to mock UX and telemetry widgets (marta + console-team), (3) quota/accounting hooks (liam), (4) security review for signature scheme (security). aim for staging rollout next week.

raj: i'll drop a short RFC with the edge config and the signature header format. quick sketch of the signed header flow: client -> edge strips any x-experiment -> console issues a signed override token (exp, actor, route-id) -> edge verifies signature and injects x-experiment + x-override-{actor,expiry} for the router to consume.

console-team: thanks — please include an example payload for the signed token in the RFC.

jessica: thanks all. tagging @console-team to keep sync. :thumbsup:
